newsitem.title: NORWAY: Deutsche Bank says no buy-out of Sysdeco.
newsitem.headline: Deutsche Bank says no buy-out of Sysdeco.

text.p: Deutsche Bank AG said on Friday neither it nor its subsidiary Morgan Grenfell Asset Management Ltd (MGAM) planned to take over Norwegian software house Sysdeco Group ASA.
In a statement to the Oslo bourse, Deutsche Bank said it owned about 26.7 percent of Sysdeco's issued share capital and MGAM around 24.5 percent.
Deutsche Bank said its Sysdeco Shares were not be managed by MGAM or any of its subsidiaries. Altogether Deutsche Bank and its MGAM subsidiary own 51 percent of Sysdeco.
Under Norwegian securities regulations, a company is obliged to make an offer to the remaining shareholders once it has acquired 45 percent or more of the issued equity in a concern.
Morgan Grenfell issued a statement to the Oslo bourse on Thursday saying that enquiries into three of its investment funds had revealed the share holding.
The bourse transferred Sysdeco to the observation list following the fund manager's announcement.
Three MGAM funds -- MG European Growth Trust, MG Europa and Dublin-listed MG European Capital Growth -- are under investigation by British authorities for alleged irregularities.

"The original acquisition of these shareholdings, together totalling approximately 51 per cent of Sysdeco's issued share capital, had not received appropriate internal authorisations," the statement said.

"It is not the intention of Deutsche Bank AG or MGAM that any company in the Deutsche Bank group should make an offer for all the shares in Sysdeco not owned by Deutsche Bank AG or funds managed by MGAM, unless required to do so by law."
Based on preliminary advice, the bank said it did not expect that it would be required to make an offer, but it would take further legal advice.
